capitals.name: Rajagriha (Girivraja, modern Rajgir)
capitals.note: 'its first capital was Rajagriha (modern day Rajgir), then Pataliputra (modern Patna)'; 'Rajagriha was initially known as Girivrijja'. The Haryanka page has the capital shifted to Pataliputra 'during the reign of Udayin', after this dossier ends.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 5,040 km2 disc (20 cells, bbox 84.57-85.36E 25.11-25.86N, centroid 84.99E 25.49N) does not hold the page's Magadha: the capital Rajagriha (Rajgir, 85.42E 25.03N) lies about 44 km outside it, Gaya district is missing, 5 of its 20 cells lie north of 25.62N on the Vaishali bank across the Ganga, and it reaches west of the Son (to 84.51E). The page: 'The core of the kingdom was the area of Bihar south of the Ganges'; 'The territory of the initial Magadha kingdom thus corresponded to the modern-day Patna and Gaya districts'; 'bounded to the north, west, and east respectively by the Gaṅgā, Son, and Campā rivers, and the eastern spurs of the Vindhya mountains formed its southern border'. Correction: Patna 45 km + Rajgir 35 km + Gaya 45 km, cut by a polygon that follows the Ganga on the north (25.62N at 84.85E falling to 25.30N at 86.2E), the Son on the west (84.85E) and the Vindhya spurs on the south (24.3N); the circles end near 85.7E, so the east is left open until the -530 keyframe. Resolved in the gazetteer: 35 cells, about 9,100 km2 (1.8 times the disc), one piece, 5.7 km from Rajgir. The infobox has no area, so the area check is not possible; the size follows from the two districts the page names. Corrected after the adversarial review of 2026-10-18. The gazetteer's 'Magadha' region (Patna 120 km + Gaya 80 km, about 51,000 km2) is the later, larger Magadha and is not used.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria repeats the -600 disc from -530. The Mahajanapadas page has 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara' ('This was the one and only conquest of Bimbisara'), and the Bimbisara page 'The campaign was successful, Anga was annexed, and prince Kunika (Ajatashatru) was appointed governor at Champa' (no year on either), so from -530 the shape is the corrected core, the stretch to the Campā and the Anga country; the Anga dossier (sa-01-a) asks for this gain in -530. The first version of this keyframe resolved to two islands (the disc of 20 cells and Anga plus Bhagalpur 60 km of 59 cells) with about 76 km of unowned land between Rajgir and the Anga cells, although the Magadha page makes the Campā Magadha's eastern border, i.e. the two countries touch. The correction adds the stretch along the south bank of the Ganga (polygon 85.6-86.6E, 25.0-25.4N, 13 new cells, about 3,400 km2, up to the Anga land at Munger) as a separate gain from nobody; the whole is 107 cells, about 28,200 km2, one piece. The year -530 is the Anga dossier's: both the Mahajanapadas and the Bimbisara pages leave the annexation undated, so it is confidence 1 in the ledger.

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Magadha, ruled from Rajagriha, appears as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the 'Patna and Gaya districts', bounded by the Ganga, Son and Campā. The page dates no founding ('the legendary Brihadratha dynasty was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha'); -600 is Cliopatria's start, so the date is a bridge. The land is the corrected core (Cliopatria's disc missed Rajgir and Gaya).

ledger.note: Early 6th century BCE: Anga and Magadha fight over Magadha. Bimbisara 'led a military campaign against Anga, perhaps to avenge his father's earlier defeat at the hands of its king, Brahmadatta'; the Anga page (as quoted in the Anga dossier, sa-01-a, not opened here) has 'Under Dadhivahana's rule, Anga had conquered its western neighbour, the state of Magadha'. Neither page gives a year, so, as the Anga dossier does, the struggle is drawn as a contest over the Magadha core from -600 until Bimbisara's accession.

544: Bimbisara founds the Haryanka dynasty at Rajagriha. The Haryanka page: 'Established: 544 BCE', 'Bimbisara is considered to be the founder of the dynasty', 'Bimbisara reigned from 544 to 492 BCE, according to the Mahavamsa chronology'; the Magadha page's infobox has 'c. 544 - c. 413 BCE: Haryanka dynasty', its text 'c. 543 to 413 BCE', and it cites Sarao's later chronology (Bimbisara 'c.457-405 BCE'), so the year is conventional. Same state, new dynasty: no land changes.

ledger.note: 543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne ('r. 543 – 492 BCE or r. 457 – 405 BCE') and Magadha is Anga's no longer. The page gives no date for Magadha's recovery, so the contest is closed at his accession as in the Anga dossier.

ledger.note: c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara annexes Anga. 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara.' / 'This was the one and only conquest of Bimbisara.' The Magadha page agrees without a date ('Magadha expanded to include most of Bihar and Bengal with the conquest of Vajjika League and Anga, respectively'). The Bimbisara page (opened in the repair) agrees and is also silent on the year: 'The campaign was successful, Anga was annexed, and prince Kunika (Ajatashatru) was appointed governor at Champa.' The year -530 is the Anga dossier's (sa-01-a); confidence stays 1.

notes: One state in two Cliopatria rows: this Janapada of Magadha (-600..-501) and 'Magadha - Haryanka dynasty' (-500..-405) are the same Magadha (the Haryanka page makes the dynasty start in 544 BCE, inside this row); the Haryanka dossier (another sa-01 part) should treat -500 as continuity, and the colour agent should give both one colour. The Anga annexation is carried here at -530 on the Anga dossier's date; the Bimbisara article, opened in the repair run, confirms the annexation but gives no year, so it stays at confidence 1; the Anga dossier carries the matching dissolve. Repair of 2026-10-18 (after the adversarial review): the -600 core is no longer Cliopatria's disc (which missed Rajgir and Gaya and crossed the Ganga and the Son) but the Patna-Gaya core cut to the page's bounds; the -530 shape adds a stretch along the Ganga's south bank so that Magadha and Anga touch (gain from nobody); the Anga-Magadha wars are mirrored from the Anga dossier (contest -600..-543, confidence 1), whose zone is still Cliopatria's Magadha disc. Not in the ledger because the pages give no year: Bimbisara's Kosala marriage with the Kasi village as dowry (Kosala page, Kasi page) and his marriage to Chellana (Haryanka page); both are single villages or no land. The Vajjika conquest (Malla page: war declared 484, League beaten by 468 BCE) and the Kosala conquest fall after this row ends and are carried in the Malla and Kosala dossiers and by the Haryanka dossier. The pages disagree on Bimbisara's dates (544-492 Mahavamsa; Keay 'late 5th century'; Sarao 457-405), so every Magadha year before the shapes is conventional. Pages: Magadha, Haryanka dynasty and the shared Mahajanapadas page (budget 1-2 plus the shared page). Gazetteer: all names used exist.
